translations.text: In the days when the judges ruled, a famine came upon the land. A man went from Bethlehem in Judah to live in the countryside of Moab, with his wife and his children.
They took Moabite wives for themselves. One was named Orpah, and the other was named Ruth. They lived there for about ten years.
Naomi said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and her gods. You too should return with your sister-in-law.”
“I went away full, but the Lord brought me back empty. Why do you call me Naomi, when the Lord has humbled me and caused me such great suffering?”
Boaz said to Ruth, “Have you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and do not leave this place. Instead, stay close to my young women.”
“May the Lord reward you for what you have done. May you receive your full reward from the Lord, the God of Israel, to whom you have come to find refuge under his wings.”
Ruth said to him, “I have found favor in your eyes, for you have made me glad and comforted the heart of your servant. Look, I will be like one of your servant women.”

Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by the Lord, for he has not abandoned his kindness toward the living and the dead.” Naomi also said, “The man is our close relative, one of our kinsmen.”
Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “It is good, my daughter, that you stay close to his young women, so that they do not find you in another field.”
He said to her, “Who are you?” She answered him, “I am Ruth, your servant. Cover me with the edge of your garment, for you are a kinsman.”
She said, “He gave me these six measures of barley, for he told me, ‘Do not return empty-handed to your mother-in-law.’”
Naomi took the child, laid him in her lap, and became his nurse.
These are the descendants of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron.
